2. The plaintiff filed the suit for partition of the suit property claiming 8 annas share by metes and bounds and for khas possession and for accounts form 1.3.72 till filling of the suit. Abdul Gafur, Abdul Bari and Abdul Karim were three full brothers who owned joint properties including the homestead at Karimganj Town, a motor workshop, a rice mill, three service motor buses and one motor Taxi, one vulcanizing machine, one battery charging machine and some other assets Each brother had 1/3rd share in joint family properties and business. Abdul Gafur died leaving behind plaintiff No. 1 as son, who was a minor at that time and plaintiff No. 2 as widow. When Abdul Gafur died plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 were living along with Abdul Gafur's brother Abdul Bari who used to manage the joint family business and the properties although. The surviving brothers Abdul Bari and Abdul Karim made a reference to an Arbitrator, namely. Moulvi Abdur Raquib on 30.3.48 for partition of their properties, The Arbitrator settled the dispute between the brothers and made an award on 16.7.48 Accordingly Abdul Karim's 1/3rd share was separated and the remaining 2/3rd share remained jointly with Abdul Bari and the plaintiffs. The award was not made the rule of the court but it was implemented by the parties amicably. After the communal riot of 1950 at Karimganj Abdul Bari along with the plaintiffs migrated to Sylhet and Abdul Bari brought two service buses which sell in their share to Sylhet. The said buses were renumbered as Sylhet "BA-228" and Sylhet "BA-475", The said bus business was a very profitable one and Abdul Bari earned a lot of money out of that bus business, Abdul Bari also brought to this country Vulcanizing machine, battery charging machine and all tools and implements of the motor workshop. Other items such as Rice Mill, the motor Taxi and homestead at Karimganj were sold at Karimganj and Abdul Bari brought the sale proceed to this country. The plaintiffs lived with Abdul Bari in joint mess and property till December, 1971 when the plaintiffs became separated in mess, but the properties remained in ejmali. After the marriage of plaintiff No.1 the plaintiff constructed a building with pucca wall and other rooms in Schedule 2 property. Abdul Bari also constructed a building in schedule 2 property with joint family funds. Abdul Bari died in October, 1972 leaving defendant Nos, 1-14 as his legal heirs. It is further asserted that during his life-time Abdul Bari purchased land of schedule 2 with the fund of joint family. Hence, the plaintiffs claimed 8 annas share in the suit properties. Abdul Bari purchased from Sylhet Co-operative Land Mortgage Bank Ltd. ST schedule I and schedule 2 properties with the joint family funds. The plaintiffs bonafide believed that the properties were purchased in the joint names. The plaintiffs demanded partition and defendant Nos. 1-5 refused partition. On inquiry the plaintiffs came to know that Abdul Bari surreptitiously got a deed of transfer of property in the name of defendant No.1 though the properties were all purchased with the joint funds of the joint business. According to the plaintiffs the consideration money for the suit property was paid fully by Abdul Bari from out of the funds of the joint family and as such they are claiming 8 annas share in the suit property. 

 3. Defendant No.1 Rabeya Khanom Chowdhury widow of Abdul Bari and defendant No.5 Azizul Bari Chowdhury son of Abdul Bari contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. According to the contesting defendants the said Abdul Bari acquired the landed property and established the business with his own money and his other brothers Abdul Gafur and Abdul karim could not make any substantial earning. The property of the defendants were not purchased from out of the joint funds of any joint business. The schedule property separate property of the defendants. The Arbitration award having not been made a rule of the court it has got no legal effect and the award was not acted upon by parties. Their further case is that during the communal riot in 1950 at Karimganj Town, Abdul Bari along with his family members came to Sylhet for safety of their lives leaving behind their service buses, vulcanizing machines and factory. The suit house was purchased by defendant No. 1 on 7.11. 55 out of her own fund and on taking loan from Bath Ali, husband of her sister. They denied that the two buses were brought from karimganj and the properties were purchased out of the earning of joint family business. It is further asserted in the written statement that the plaintiffs have got no right in the suit property and the plaintiffs were allowed to reside in Schedule 2 property as licensee.
